newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat planting makes good progress.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat planting makes good progress.

text.p: Mostly dry weather kept Oklahoma producers active planting small grains and harvesting row crops during the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly state crop report.
"Producers in many areas were preparing wheat ground that had previously been too wet," the report said. "Replanting was also active in areas that previous...rains had washed out."
Armyworms and leafhoppers continued to pose problems in many areas, the report said.
Wheat planting advanced to 74 percent, versus last year's pace of 58 percent and the five-year average of 76 percent.
Wheat up-to-stand 35 percent vs 20 y/a, 38 avge
Corn harvested 79 percent vs 67 y/a, 89 avge.
Corn mature 90 percent vs 93 y/a, 98 avge.
Sorghum harvested 18 percent vs 11 y/a, 16 avge.
Sorghum mature 53 percent vs 35 y/a, 52 avge.
Soybeans harvested 38 percent vs 33 y/a, 30 avge.
Soybeans mature 78 pct vs 59 y/a, 66 avge.
Soybeans rated 66 pct good to excellent, 28 fair, 6 poor.
Cotton bolls opening 66 percent vs 32 y/a, 61 avge.
Cotton harvested 4 percent vs nil y/a, 13 avge.
Pasture and range condition was rated 78 pct good to excellent.
